tasks.short: Arrange and administer job-relevant assessments for applicants or employees.

steps.what: Confirm assessment necessity, permitted scope and qualified provider requirements.
Arrange participant, room and provider availability and send assessment instructions.
Agree assessment adjustments and explain the procedure to the participant.
Verify identity, explain instructions and supervise the assessment session.
Retrieve permitted results from the assessment platform and match them to the participant.
Review invalid sessions, unexpected results and requests for reassessment.
Record completion and notify the hiring manager of the permitted disposition.

tasks.design: Configure bookings, instructions and reminders through the {WORKFLOW}, {CALENDAR} and {EMAIL}, after a person approves the assessment scope. A deterministic connector transfers permitted assessment status from the assessment platform in {OTHER} to the {ATS} or {HCM}; qualified people administer restricted tests and decide reassessment cases.
tasks.previous_blocker: Scheduling crossed several calendars and provider interfaces. Sensitive results required careful access boundaries, while suitability and adjustments needed human judgement.
tasks.enabler_now: Existing booking and approval features handle much of the coordination. AI-assisted coding makes narrow connectors cheaper to build; no model loop is needed for this design.
tasks.still_hard: Provider interfaces, reasonable adjustments and restricted assessments remain costly. Health data needs an appropriate GDPR basis and access controls; national rules govern which tests are permitted.
tasks.human_edge: Explain a sensitive assessment, recognise an unfair testing condition and challenge an unnecessary test.

ambition.what: Pre-assessment adjustment consultation for applicants needing an accessible testing format

tasks.altitude: The week contains fewer bookings and result transfers, leaving more time for adjustments and assessment quality. No additional hiring or clinical decision rights arise automatically.

reach.task: Arrange skills assessments for internal development programmes
reach.learn: Accessible assessment formats, assessment validity and the distinction between development and selection

evidence.claim: Booking, reminders and completion records can use configured workflows and deterministic integrations.
AI used to evaluate recruitment candidates or workers can fall within high-risk employment categories.
GDPR restricts solely automated decisions with legal or similarly significant effects.
In the Netherlands, works council consent can apply to HR-data and monitoring arrangements; national rules elsewhere vary.

assumptions: Skills assessments are the common case; psychological and drug tests are conditional, specialist activities.
Clinical testing is performed by qualified providers; HR receives only information it is entitled to receive.
The steps describe applicant assessments. Employee assessments use the same pattern with {HCM} and employee-lifecycle.
Time shares estimate active handling effort, excluding participant time and provider waiting time.
The supplied priors support automating coordination while retaining assessment judgement and personal support.
Build ranges are working-day effort for one assessment route; consultation may take longer in elapsed time.
unknowns: Which assessment types are used, and for which roles?
Which provider interfaces and booking features are available?
Who may access each result type, and what retention periods apply?
Which national rules and employee consultation requirements apply?
How many assessments require supervision or adjustments?
research_questions: Can provider completion status be transferred without transferring detailed sensitive results?
Which existing booking features cover rescheduling and accessible assessment formats?
Which assessments can be removed because they add no defensible job-relevant evidence?
new_work: Handle booking failures and participant identity mismatches.
Check permissions and retention jobs for assessment records.
Maintain instructions, provider mappings and adjustment routes.
Review whether each assessment remains necessary.

tasks.short: Check applicant references and relevant background evidence before hiring.

steps.what: Choose proportionate checks and confirm legal grounds, notices and required permissions.
Collect reference contacts and required background documents from the candidate.
Send authorised reference requests and chase missing responses.
Verify referee identity and discuss relevant evidence using a structured reference call.
Compare application claims with reference evidence and flag discrepancies.

loop.input: Application claims and authorised reference evidence, with verified source identities.
loop.output: A source-linked evidence table and possible discrepancies; no hiring recommendation.
loop.check: Validate dates deterministically; require source passages for claims and human verification of material discrepancies.
loop.stop: One extraction pass and one repair pass per evidence bundle; unresolved or unsupported items go to HR.
loop.why_not_simpler: Structured forms cover routine facts, but reference letters and call notes express dates and qualifications inconsistently.

steps.what: Resolve material discrepancies with the candidate and approve the check outcome.

tasks.design: Configure candidate forms, authorised requests, reminders and check status in the {ATS} and {WORKFLOW}. A bounded loop compares unstructured evidence from the {DOCS} with application claims and produces a source-linked table; HR verifies referees, hears explanations and approves the check outcome.
tasks.previous_blocker: Requests and evidence were scattered across the {EMAIL}, {DOCS} and {ATS}. Reference wording varied, and discrepancies could not safely be treated as automatic failures.
tasks.enabler_now: Configured forms remove much of the chasing and copying. A small bounded loop can assemble cited evidence, while deterministic checks handle dates, missing fields and status.
tasks.still_hard: Referee authenticity, evasive answers and disputed histories need personal investigation. Criminal and other restricted background data require specific legal conditions under GDPR and national rules; employee or applicant consent alone may be insufficient.
tasks.human_edge: Distinguish an innocent mismatch from material misrepresentation and give the applicant a fair opportunity to explain.

ambition.what: Pre-decision discrepancy clarification for applicants with conflicting employment records

tasks.altitude: The week shifts from chasing and assembling evidence to reference conversations and disputed cases. HR gains no automatic right to reject candidates or expand background-check scope.

reach.task: Review whether background checks create unjustified barriers to employment
reach.learn: Job relevance, proportionality, discrimination risks and fair candidate challenge procedures

evidence.claim: Forms, reminders and check-status records can be automated without automating hiring decisions.
A bounded model loop can draft a source-linked comparison of unstructured reference evidence.
GDPR restricts solely automated decisions with legal or similarly significant effects.
AI that evaluates candidates for recruitment can fall within the AI Act's high-risk employment category.
Restricted background information requires legal grounds and safeguards beyond a general permission form.

assumptions: Checks are limited to documented, job-relevant requirements.
The supplied gathering-heavy priors support automating collection, while calls and disputed evidence remain human.
External requests use approved templates and scope; unusual requests return to HR.
The loop supports evidence preparation and never ranks applicants.
Time shares are illustrative active-effort estimates, not measured company data.
Build ranges cover one check process and working-day effort; consultation and referee responses add elapsed time.
unknowns: Which checks are mandatory or permitted for each role?
Which candidate forms, request templates and status features already exist?
How are referee identity and document authenticity verified?
Who decides disputed outcomes, and can candidates challenge them?
Which data categories, retention rules and national consultation requirements apply?
research_questions: Which requested checks can be removed without losing necessary job-relevant assurance?
Can routine reference facts be collected through structured responses?
How accurately does source-linked comparison identify discrepancies without converting missing evidence into adverse findings?
new_work: Verify source passages and material discrepancy flags.
Handle undelivered requests, missing evidence and contested records.
Maintain request scope, templates and retention rules.
Sample comparisons for omissions and misleading summaries.

tasks.short: Verify applicants' professional credentials against role-specific eligibility requirements.

steps.what: Gather required credentials and identify the applicable professional eligibility rules.
Check credential status and identity against authoritative professional registers.
Read certificates for qualification, restrictions, issuer and expiry details.

loop.input: Credential documents and available authoritative verification records.
loop.output: Qualification, issuer, identifier, restrictions and expiry, with supporting document passages.
loop.check: Validate schema and dates; match identifiers to verified records and show uncertain fields for review.
loop.stop: One extraction pass and one repair pass per document; unreadable or conflicting fields require human entry.
loop.why_not_simpler: Official structured records are preferred, but some certificates arrive as scans or varied document formats.

steps.what: Compare verified facts with required qualifications, restrictions and validity dates.
Clarify equivalence, missing evidence and disputed restrictions with the candidate or licensing authority.
Approve internal eligibility clearance or hold and record the supporting evidence.

tasks.design: The {WORKFLOW} gathers credentials into the {ATS}, while deterministic connectors retrieve available register evidence from the {GOV_PORTAL} or {PARTNER_PORTAL}. A bounded extraction loop handles document-only credentials, then versioned rules produce an eligibility checklist; HR approves internal clearance and refers statutory licensing decisions to the competent authority.
tasks.previous_blocker: Register access was fragmented, certificates varied and eligibility rules were often buried in documents. Foreign qualifications and restrictions required interpretation.
tasks.enabler_now: Small connectors and versioned rule tables are cheaper to build with AI-assisted coding. Document extraction can now be bounded and checked against authoritative evidence.
tasks.still_hard: Register coverage, identity matching and foreign-qualification equivalence remain difficult. National licensing and employment rules determine what HR can conclude; an internal checklist cannot award a licence.
tasks.human_edge: Recognise when a credential is formally valid but insufficient for the actual role, and seek an authoritative interpretation.

ambition.what: Early credential-gap advice for applicants with overseas qualifications

tasks.altitude: The week shifts from reading certificates and checking dates to equivalence cases and applicant guidance. HR gains no statutory licensing authority; internal clearance rights remain delegated by the employer.

reach.task: Plan development needed to close a professional credential gap
reach.learn: Recognised qualification routes, supervised-practice requirements and limits on equivalence decisions

evidence.claim: Structured credential facts can be checked against explicit eligibility rules using deterministic code.
Document extraction can prepare credential facts but cannot establish authenticity without independent evidence.
AI used to evaluate recruitment candidates can fall within a high-risk employment category.
GDPR restrictions matter when an eligibility result determines a legally or similarly significant decision.

assumptions: In a typical company, this task means checking eligibility for regulated work, rather than issuing statutory licences.
The employer has approved role-specific requirements before an individual case starts.
At least one authoritative register supports permitted structured access; unsupported registers retain manual checking.
The strong rule-coverage prior supports deterministic comparison, while equivalence and disputed evidence remain human.
Time shares are illustrative; register accessibility strongly affects the savings.
Build ranges cover one regulated role family, not a universal international credential service.
Consultation and access ranges describe working-day effort, not guaranteed elapsed approval time.
unknowns: Which roles require licences or regulated qualifications?
Which authoritative registers support permitted access?
Which national rules govern equivalence, restrictions and licence validity?
Who has delegated authority to approve internal clearance?
How often do overseas, expired or disputed credentials occur?
Does the company actually perform statutory licensing work?
research_questions: Which required facts are already available from authoritative structured records?
How should each rule version be linked to a historical clearance decision?
Can expiry and restriction checks be implemented without interpreting free text?
Which exceptions require an external authority rather than an HR judgement?
new_work: Review uncertain extracted fields and identity matches.
Maintain eligibility rules, effective dates and register connectors.
Handle unavailable registers and changed access conditions.
Audit clearances against their original evidence and rule versions.

tasks.short: Evaluate selection criteria against job relevance, testing standards and fair recruitment requirements.

steps.what: Define the role groups, criteria and professional standards to review.
Export selection-stage results and assemble permitted outcome data.
Calculate selection rates, missingness, reliability and relevant outcome associations.
Assess job relevance, statistical limitations and conformance to professional testing standards.
Write proposed criterion changes with supporting evidence and implementation implications.

loop.input: Human-approved findings, calculated results and versioned professional standards.
loop.output: A revision proposal linking each proposed change to a finding and supporting source.
loop.check: Check quoted numbers against calculated results; verify citations and have HR review every recommendation.
loop.stop: One draft and one revision pass per review; unsupported recommendations are removed or written by HR.
loop.why_not_simpler: A template supplies structure, but explaining role-specific trade-offs requires prose grounded in varied findings.

steps.what: Agree revisions with hiring stakeholders and approve changes to live selection criteria.

tasks.design: A governed job on the {DATA_PLATFORM} joins permitted data from the {ATS} and {HCM}, runs a fixed analysis specification and feeds a {BI} review dashboard. A bounded loop drafts proposals in the {DOCS} from verified findings; the HR manager approves any change to live criteria in the {ATS}.
tasks.previous_blocker: Data linkage and repeated analysis took substantial effort. Small samples, changing roles and disputed standards made automatic recommendations unreliable.
tasks.enabler_now: AI-assisted coding makes reusable extraction and analysis pipelines cheaper to build. The model is limited to drafting from checked findings; calculations and release controls remain deterministic.
tasks.still_hard: Selection bias, small samples and weak outcome measures limit conclusions. Professional validation may need a qualified testing specialist; protected-group analysis needs lawful data use, and national rules govern consultation and discrimination duties.
tasks.human_edge: Judge whether a statistically convenient criterion measures the work fairly and persuade stakeholders to revise a familiar practice.

ambition.what: Monthly selection-criteria review for high-volume role families

tasks.altitude: The week contains less dataset assembly and repeated arithmetic, with more time for testing validity and stakeholder decisions. HR can recommend monthly reviews; authority to release new criteria remains with the HR manager.

reach.task: Investigate whether selection practices create unjustified group disparities
reach.learn: Lawful group analysis, statistical uncertainty, job relevance and discrimination assessment

reach.role: Compensation, Benefits, and Job Analysis Specialists
reach.task: Connect selection criteria to documented job demands
reach.learn: Job-analysis methods and evidence connecting assessment content to actual work

evidence.claim: Reusable deterministic analysis can reduce repeated dataset assembly and arithmetic in selection reviews.
AFAS Profit 8 scores applications per vacancy; this demonstrates scoring capability, not validity or fairness.
Textkernel parses CVs and supports applicant matching; this does not establish compliance of selection criteria.
Recruitment and worker-evaluation AI are included in the AI Act's high-risk employment categories.
In the Netherlands, works council consent can apply to HR-data and monitoring arrangements; other national rules vary.
A determining score can fall within GDPR automated-decision restrictions.

assumptions: This is a review of selection practices, not an automated applicant-ranking service.
Only lawfully available data is used; protected characteristics are not inferred from names, images or CVs.
The judgement-heavy, low-drudgery priors support retaining standards assessment and approval with people.
The spreadsheet step reflects common analytical glue between the {ATS} and {HCM}, not a replacement for their operational records.
Analyses display uncertainty and suppress groups under an approved disclosure policy.
Time shares are illustrative; specialist validation work may increase the human share.
Build ranges cover one role family and an agreed analysis specification, including working-day consultation effort.
Legal treatment depends on the tool's actual purpose and use; preparation-only automation does not by itself establish a high-risk classification.
unknowns: Which criteria and assessments are currently used?
Are selection-stage records complete and consistently defined?
Can recruitment records lawfully be linked to employee outcomes?
Are appropriate group data available, and under what legal conditions?
Who has statistical and professional testing expertise?
Which consultation procedures and national rules apply?
Who approves live criteria, and how are changes versioned?
research_questions: Which analysis methods fit the available sample sizes and outcome measures?
How much observed disparity reflects data quality, job differences or selection effects?
Which criteria lack evidence connecting them to actual job demands?
Can an existing {BI} configuration provide the required analysis and disclosure controls?
new_work: Maintain dataset definitions, linkage controls and analysis specifications.
Review missingness, sample sizes and disclosure risks.
Verify proposal citations, calculations and recommendations.
Record approved criterion versions and evaluate their subsequent effects.
Arrange specialist validation when the evidence exceeds HR's expertise.

role.altitude: The HR specialist spends less time booking, chasing, copying and calculating, and more time on applicant explanations, credential exceptions and assessment quality. Hiring, restricted-testing and statutory licensing authority do not expand automatically; delegated rights must be explicit.
reach: Training and Development Specialists: turn verified skills and credential gaps into appropriate development routes.
Equal Opportunity Representatives and Officers: investigate fairness concerns in checks and selection criteria.
Compensation, Benefits, and Job Analysis Specialists: connect assessments to documented job requirements.
Human Resources Managers: present evidence-backed proposals for approved changes to selection practices.
skills_to_grow: Translate policies into testable rules and exception routes.
Validate source-linked evidence without over-trusting summaries.
Interpret statistical uncertainty and assessment validity.
Handle sensitive applicant conversations and reasonable adjustments.
Apply GDPR, relevant AI Act duties and national employment rules.
Specify access, retention and decision authority for connected workflows.
role.ambitious_version: Provide early, accessible assessment guidance and credential-gap advice, while running monthly evidence-based reviews of high-volume selection processes. Keep consequential decisions with authorised people who can explain and challenge the evidence.
